tr.td: Primary care visit for headaches, fatigue, and a very high blood pressure
One-week blood pressure and kidney safety check with nephrology consultation

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Treat severe hypertension without acute target-organ damage as an outpatient: start losartan and amlodipine together, check home blood pressure twice daily, and go to the emergency department for chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness, confusion, or vision loss
Nephrology referral for eGFR below 60 with severely increased albuminuria (UACR above 300 mg/g) and stage 2 hypertension
Titrate losartan to the maximum tolerated dose and add an SGLT2 inhibitor for CKD with UACR of at least 200 mg/g; accept a creatinine rise of up to 30 percent
Add chlorthalidone if blood pressure stays above target on two agents; avoid NSAIDs and review every medication dose for kidney function

Check potassium and creatinine one to four weeks after each renin-angiotensin, SGLT2 inhibitor, or diuretic change; then eGFR and UACR about three times a year for G3b A3, hemoglobin at least yearly, and calcium, phosphate, and PTH every six to twelve months; recalculate the kidney failure risk yearly
Moderate-intensity statin for an adult aged 50 or older with eGFR below 60; no routine repeat LDL
Sodium below 2 g a day with a plan for meals while traveling; at least 150 minutes of activity a week
Annual dilated eye examination for hypertensive retinopathy; pneumococcal and hepatitis B vaccination for chronic kidney disease
Lower blood pressure below 130/80 within two months
Reach a standardized office systolic pressure below 120 when tolerated by the six-month review
Reduce the urine albumin-creatinine ratio by at least 30 percent by the six-month review
Keep eGFR decline after starting therapy within 30 percent and stable thereafter
eGFR 36 at baseline, 30 on full therapy, 32 at six months
